catalog_quote: 1.3 Stress. Word stress in Ifira-Mele falls regularly on the antepenultimate vowel, with long vowels treated as two vowels for the purpose of stress assignment. A normal utterance must contain at least three vowels. Speakers will not cite nouns and verbs with just two vowels (including many of the most common words in the language) in isolation, but always with an article, verb prefix or other affix attached.

audit.reasoning: Quote check: both deciding quotations are present verbatim at the stated places in held files (Clark 2002 p. 682 sec. 1.3 in the scanned text of The Oceanic Languages; Clark 1998 PL C-149 p. x). Deciding source: a 2002 grammar sketch plus a 1998 dictionary introduction, both by Ross Clark, the only linguist to have done sustained fieldwork on Mele; Glottolog lists no grammar, phonology monograph, dissertation or instrumental study for mele1250, and Clark himself says no comprehensive description exists. The coding (antepenultimate vowel/mora, long vowels count double -> weight-sensitive right-edge, CVV heavy) follows directly from the quoted rule.
